dialogues.speaker: Su Ding
dialogues.text: Each round of the tabletop Wargame provides valuable intel that can be used as a reference for enhancing the overall security of Teyvat. The more info we have, the better, so please feel free to let your tactical acumen run wild.

choices.text: I'll play a few more rounds then.

response.speaker: Su Ding
response.text: Excellent. The board will be reset after each Wargame, so you can start over whenever you like.

choices.text: About this Wargame...

response.speaker: Su Ding
response.text: Lord Kaiyang proposed holding this Wargame to Lady Tianquan. It is a trial conference of limited scope, but it should be sufficient to assess the veracity of utilizing miniaturized simulations to obtain intelligence.

response.speaker: Su Ding
response.text: Lady Yuheng sent letters of invitation to the armed services of our neighboring nations in order to deepen our cooperation, introduce new variables, and expand the intel that the exercise could provide.

response.speaker: Su Ding
response.text: Improving the security of our neighbors can also reduce the risk of merchant caravans being attacked on the road, which will in turn be beneficial for expanding the scale of commercial relations.

response.speaker: Su Ding
response.text: Naturally, cooperation will be limited to an appropriate level. The Millelith will not share the means at our disposal for protecting our homeland, and the other armies all have their own unique capabilities.

response.speaker: Su Ding
response.text: This is part of the reason that no gamepieces modeled after any of our own combat units are among those to be used in the wargame. After all, the primary objective of the simulation is to assess schools of thought related to formations and deployment.

response.speaker: Su Ding
response.text: Building mutual trust, finding common ground, and working together for the betterment of all are what I understand to be the goals of our cooperation.

choices.text: Tell me about yourself...

response.speaker: Su Ding
response.text: Our paths have crossed before, but it is unlikely you paid me much heed.

response.speaker: Su Ding
response.text: I was once a frontline soldier, and followed Lady Yuheng to the Guyun Stone Forest to deploy our mass-produced Guizhong Ballistae against Beisht's attack.

response.speaker: Su Ding
response.text: I personally witnessed the entire battle in which you and Adeptus Shenhe repelled Beisht. It was profoundly moving.

choices.text: That kinda rings a bell...

response.speaker: Su Ding
response.text: I am honored. It seems you are blessed with an eidetic memory. Nothing less than should be expected of such a matchless commander.

response.speaker: Su Ding
response.text: In any case, it is difficult for mere mortals to defeat foes on that level by relying solely on improving the martial skills or weapons of a single individual.

response.speaker: Su Ding
response.text: That is not to discount the importance of those two factors, or that one can be prepared for everything simply by sticking to traditional army formations. But we must adapt to the times and continually upgrade our arsenal and tactics.

response.speaker: Su Ding
response.text: Combining advanced weaponry and tactics are the basic requirements for securing victory. Utilizing the proper tactics for the adversary you are facing is the key to prevailing.

response.speaker: Su Ding
response.text: The significance of this Wargame lies in acquiring more of these "keys." With sufficient preparation, even an enemy as powerful as Beisht can be dealt with.

choices.text: Sorry, I'm drawing a blank...

response.speaker: Su Ding
response.text: No matter. Past experiences are peripheral to the main point.

choices.text: Adeptus Shenhe...

response.speaker: Su Ding
response.text: Her adeptal power is worthy of utmost veneration. But it may be beyond the capacity of an ordinary soldier to acquire such strength through honing their martial skills...

choices.text: Regarding the other armies taking part...

response.speaker: Su Ding
response.text: You want to hear my opinion of the armed forces of our neighbors? Then I'll be frank—

response.speaker: Su Ding
response.text: They are all top-notch professionals of the highest caliber.

response.speaker: Su Ding
response.text: The representative from the Knights of Favonius is an intelligence officer, skilled in using cutting-edge Alchemical technology to engage in remote reconnaissance.

response.speaker: Su Ding
response.text: However, if you wish to exploit the advantage offered by such distance reconnaissance, corresponding projectile weapons must also be purchased and logistics units for delivering the associated material organized, all of which require a considerable budget...

response.speaker: Su Ding
response.text: The Shogunate representative is from the Yashiro Commission, and has outstanding swordsmanship. He courageously leads his troops from the front, and his drive in battle is truly commendable.

response.speaker: Su Ding
response.text: However, if you are too focused on personally leading troops in an assault, it may be difficult to properly command, and you may end up winning a localized victory while the overall battle is a catastrophic defeat. One should never allow oneself to get carried away...

response.speaker: Su Ding
response.text: As for the representative from Sumeru's Corps of Thirty, he is adept at handling extreme environments from the desert to the rainforest, and claims that he and his troops can fight for an extended period of time with just a small quantity of supplies.

response.speaker: Su Ding
response.text: However, in order to increase their ability to adapt to those environments, the Corps of Thirty is a relatively lightly armed force. If they had to take on heavily armored foes directly, they could easily find themselves at a disadvantage...

response.speaker: Su Ding
response.text: The representative sent by Fontaine's Special Security and Surveillance Patrol belongs to an exceptional firearms unit. Highly organized and with strict discipline, they can accurately unleash withering volleys on any enemy.

response.speaker: Su Ding
response.text: However, their equipment is quite complex, and can be complicated to use. All this maintenance is of the utmost importance, and members must all be trained to high standards. This, in turn, makes it very difficult to substantially increase troop levels.

response.speaker: Su Ding
response.text: Ultimately, there is no such thing as a perfect combat unit. All that can be done is for the relevant personnel to try to make up for their weaknesses, and continually improve their performance in actual combat situations.

response.speaker: Su Ding
response.text: I believe that with increased communication and cooperation, we will all benefit.

choices.text: We'll talk more later!

response.speaker: Su Ding
response.text: Then I look forward to that day, and to your continued participation in the Wargames!

dialogues.speaker: Phonia
dialogues.text: We meet again, Honorary Knight. When Su Ding mentioned he planned on inviting a reliable outside expert to join us, I immediately thought of you.

choices.text: Sorry, I don't remember you very well...

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: That's fine, after all, I'm just a cog in the machine. Officers don't necessarily have to remember the name of everyone serving under them, just their positions and duties. That's enough to be able to effectively give orders.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: I'm Phonia, formerly a Signals Officer of the Investigative Team. I'm responsible for testing alchemical instruments developed by Captain Albedo and exploring the uses of remote reconnaissance technology.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: However, in light of how the Knights of Favonius have updated their tactics and the staffing structure now that some units from the expeditionary force have returned, Captain Albedo applied to have me assigned to the reorganized 7th Company.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: The 7th Company is temporarily designated as a "Combined Arms Company," which integrates knights with a range of capabilities into a single combat unit, with a balance of ranged and melee firepower. Such a unit is also very reliant on reconnaissance.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: When the time comes, the expeditionary force's No. 2 — the venerable Commander Frederica Gunnhildr might become our Company's Captain.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: After all, Commander Frederica has served for longer than many Knights have been alive, and her experience in battle is unmatched. It wouldn't be too much to say she is perfectly suited for leadership.

choices.text: Gunnhildr? That sounds familiar...

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: Correct! Commander Frederica is the Acting Grand Master's mother, and is famous throughout Mondstadt.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: She's been on active duty on the front lines for decades on end, never tiring or slowing. When the youths of Mondstadt talk of their dreams of being a hero, the name "Frederica" is never far from their lips.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: And I was one of them! When I joined the Knights of Favonius, it was because of my admiration for Commander Frederica...

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: Of course, I later realized that I was only talented enough to be just one more cog in the machine. As for the heroic protagonists of the storybooks that can take on a hundred foes all alone... that's another story.

choices.text: Jean's mother...

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: That's only my speculation as a Signals Officer. As I see it, the 7th Company will likely be one of the most formidable units, and so Commander Frederica would be the most suitable candidate for Captain.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: Though Commander Frederica's position in the Knights of Favonius long surpassed any ordinary Captain, she doesn't seem to like pushing paperwork around and insists on staying on the front lines, toe-to-toe with foes.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: In principle, the Knights of Favonius value ability and experience equally, so after she returns, perhaps we'll see the Acting Grand Master giving orders to Commander Frederica...

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: The two of them should have absolutely seamless synergy.

choices.text: Might become a Captain?
Isn't that also Jean's last name...?
I feel like I've seen you before...

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: That's right! We've met once before, while I was executing the "Annihilate the Invasive Anglers" operation.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: Since then, I've been carrying out experiments to advance alchemical detection equipment as planned, and have worked with the Reconnaissance Company and Outriders on numerous occasions.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: Over time, I slowly became a slightly more important cog in the Knights of Favonius's intelligence machine, and that's why I was chosen to participate in this event.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: Who knows, maybe the next time you return to the Knights to take on a commission, the intel I gather will be useful to you!

choices.text: How do you think the Wargame is going?

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: The thing that strikes me most is how each nation has a vastly different approach to fighting.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: Due to the different levels of focus on the size of their forces and training, the Millelith are concerned more with formations and the disposition of their troops.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: When clearing out hordes of monsters, they're like a steel-flanked juggernaut. They can just directly roll over an entire camp of the beasties, crushing everything in their path. Offense and defense all in one, completely unstoppable.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: When operating on terrain ill-suited to deploying a wide front line, they'll split up, reassembling into multiple smaller formations of the appropriate dimensions such that their flexibility to pursue their objectives isn't compromised.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: Even if an opponent studies their tactics and formations, and their intelligence is accurate, it would still be difficult to find a weakness to exploit.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: Fortunately, this style requires a very high degree of awareness and discipline from every soldier. In all of Teyvat, maybe only Liyue's Millelith can do that...

choices.text: I won't keep you any longer.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: Then we'll talk more next time, Honorary Knight.

dialogues.speaker: Turenna
dialogues.text: Turenna of the Special Security and Surveillance Patrol, reporting to Proto-Boss! Greetings! Seeing that you're participating too really makes the trip down here totally worth it!

choices.text: Since when did I become a "Proto-Boss"?

response.speaker: Turenna
response.text: Aha, that's Captain Chevreuse and Captain Grosrochard's assessment of you! The highest acknowledgment of both the Special Patrol and the Gardes!

response.speaker: Turenna
response.text: You've been promoted from "Boss-Level Force" to "Proto-Boss"! That means not only are your fighting skills up to par, but you're the cream of the crop when it comes to commanding as well!

response.speaker: Turenna
response.text: Doesn't the fact that that Staff Officer from the Millelith Su Ding invited you to join prove it?

response.speaker: Turenna
response.text: The simulation was pretty interesting! I got to see some of the greatest fighters from other countries for myself, and how they dealt with monsters was simply dazzling! It was just like all the stuff you showed me before...

response.speaker: Turenna
response.text: Oh! Sorry, I know you're a super busy bee buzzing all over, so you might not be able to remember right away!

response.speaker: Turenna
response.text: When I was playing Lil' Fungi's Fun-Tastic Fiesta before, you gave me the gift of your insight...

response.speaker: Turenna
response.text: And during the Fontinalia Film Festival, you showed me just what a real top gun could do in our Thousand-Pace Interdiction Arcminute Sharpshooting Zone promotional event. That was a genuine revelation...

response.speaker: Turenna
response.text: I've made pretty significant progress lately, and haven't had too many missions on my docket, so when Captain Chevreuse and Captain Grosrochard got the invitation, they decided to send me as a representative!

response.speaker: Turenna
response.text: The Patrol members you taught are all slowly getting better. I'm working hard to become an outstanding sharpshooter capable of helping you! Trust me, the time you spent helping wasn't wasted on me!

choices.text: Hey, give yourself some credit too...

response.speaker: Turenna
response.text: You're simply too kind, Proto-Boss! ...Anyway, I just can't thank you enough!

response.speaker: Turenna
response.text: I'll be joining in a few more simulations over the next few days! The mini-monsters they use each time are different, and it kinda feels like my brain is playing in a series of... magnificent... tactical plays!

choices.text: Then study hard and work hard, soldier!

response.speaker: Turenna
response.text: Understood, Proto-Boss! I'll do my best!

choices.text: About the Special Patrol and the simulation...

response.speaker: Turenna
response.text: Actually, this isn't our first time working with the Millelith. As you know, Lumidouce Harbor and Yilong Wharf are just across the sea from each other, so we have a longstanding working relationship to maintain order and guarantee the safety of shipping.

response.speaker: Turenna
response.text: So, after Captain Chevreuse got the letter, she was pretty stoked! After all, every time we work together, both sides learn a lot about tactics and tech from one another!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: For example?

response.speaker: Turenna
response.text: Hmm, let me think... Before, we learned about different Millelith formations with layered ranks, and so we improved our own ranked volley fire, stabilizing the rhythm of our musket volleys.

response.speaker: Turenna
response.text: And for their part, the Millelith improved their own equipment by studying our muskets, allowing them to better deal with criminals who may have smuggled in firearms or Ruin machines that utilize similar weaponry.

response.speaker: Turenna
response.text: I've heard that some Millelith smiths are researching a type of armor that consists of piecing together blocks of a specially fired type of ceramic between two pieces of a particularly sturdy hardened fabric...

response.speaker: Turenna
response.text: That way, when bullets strike the armor, they would first disintegrate upon striking the outermost layer, causing the projectile to lose its structural integrity and greatly reducing its penetrative power...

response.speaker: Turenna
response.text: As the bullet continues onward, the ceramic plate in the middle will break, absorbing the vast majority of the impact, and finally the powerless, deformed bullets will be stopped by the final layer of armor.

response.speaker: Turenna
response.text: Against muskets with a small enough caliber or light enough ammo, you could get shot at point-blank range and the bullet still might not get through!

choices.text: That sounds pretty nifty.

response.speaker: Turenna
response.text: Aha, for that you'll have to ask our Millelith friends. I expect armor like that costs a fortune, and it may be difficult to manufacture on a large scale. Also, it may be too heavy for ordinary people...

response.speaker: Turenna
response.text: Though according to legend, the Millelith that fought in the great war way, way long ago wore armor that was heavier than a Gardemek, and their weapons were comparable to naval artillery... So it probably isn't too heavy for them.

response.speaker: Turenna
response.text: And ordinary musketeers wouldn't have a chance at hitting someone as skilled as you, so you probably don't need extra protection like that!

choices.text: I want a set too!
Keep it up, I've gotta get going!

response.speaker: Turenna
response.text: Don't be a stranger, I hope we'll see each other soon!

dialogues.speaker: Sido
dialogues.text: Hello, friend of the General Mahamatra and the Flame-Mane. I represent the Corps of Thirty delegation. Allow me to extend my greetings to you.

choices.text: You know me?

response.speaker: Sido
response.text: Surely you jest! You once participated in a commercial event in Port Ormos, and assisted the Corps of Thirty in arresting a crafty criminal and his scholarly accomplice.

response.speaker: Sido
response.text: Your performance during that operation showed both wisdom and bravery, and every mercenary who heard tell of your deeds considers you the best of the best.

response.speaker: Sido
response.text: It looks like you never cease in your unsparing efforts, and the amount of criminals you've dealt with is staggering. Those two scoundrels barely even register in your memory.

choices.text: Eh, more or less.

response.speaker: Sido
response.text: That is so. We should always look ahead, the Flame-Mane often says much the same.

response.speaker: Sido
response.text: Everyone in the Corps of Thirty greatly respects the Flame-Mane. She has looked out for many of our brothers, and many of our number have followed her into battle.

response.speaker: Sido
response.text: If she had a bit more patience for paperwork and rules, then perhaps she could have come with us to visit Liyue and learn.

response.speaker: Sido
response.text: Sparring with experts with completely different styles, learning new skills, not to mention Liyue cuisine should be to her liking. Everything is new, it's quite refreshing.

choices.text: Then we'll bring her some food from Liyue next time!

response.speaker: Sido
response.text: Stop by the Citadel of Regzar when you've got some time! Feast on meat and chew the fat with the brothers of the Corps of Thirty!

choices.text: I'll invite her here when I get the chance!
No need to bring up the past.
What has the Corps of Thirty learned from the Wargame?

response.speaker: Sido
response.text: You've touched on a critical issue.

response.speaker: Sido
response.text: From our cooperation thus far, I've observed a massive gap in the "degree of organization."

response.speaker: Sido
response.text: As everyone knows, the Corps of Thirty is one branch of the many Eremite organizations. Though responsible for the defense of Sumeru's cities, the management of manpower, training, and supplies is fairly relaxed.

response.speaker: Sido
response.text: Personally, I envy the Millelith. They have a huge factory in Blackcliff Forge, and can guarantee a supply of all kinds of high-quality weapons and other equipment.

response.speaker: Sido
response.text: As mercenaries, we mostly rely on individual blacksmiths operating their own forges. We may hope to get a deal and buy a good weapon, but most can't compete with the fully finished products from Liyue's factories.

response.speaker: Sido
response.text: The Akademiya's pretty straightforward when it comes to payment, but if we were to ask them to set up a dedicated department... Everything from purchasing raw materials to production and processing... It's not likely.

response.speaker: Sido
response.text: Not to mention the Millelith provides standardized training to all their soldiers, with strict assessment standards, while most mercs are just trying to make a living. There's all levels of skill among us.

response.speaker: Sido
response.text: Anyway, in addition to tactical considerations when dealing with monsters, there're lots of other things that need to be considered.

choices.text: We'll be on our way then. Bye!

response.speaker: Sido
response.text: See you later, then. We'll talk again when you've got time.

dialogues.speaker: Kuromaro
dialogues.text: An honor to make your acquaintance, esteemed guests of the Commissioner. Having observed your distinguished person making such amiable conversation with Su Ding senpai, I hoped to be able to listen quietly and learn.

choices.text: The Commissioner?

response.speaker: Kuromaro
response.text: The name is Kuromaro, and I am at your service. I am a member of the Yashiro Commission, and it was my great honor to have heard the Commissioner and Miss Kamisato speak of your deeds.

response.speaker: Kuromaro
response.text: Courage, righteousness, etiquette, integrity, elegance, kindness, wisdom, in each of these areas, you are a role model for all to emulate.

choices.text: Is that really what Ayato and Ayaka said about me...?

response.speaker: Kuromaro
response.text: And such humility as well, this virtue too is worthy of study! If only I had the fortune to meet you sooner...

response.speaker: Kuromaro
response.text: The scale of this exchange is not large, but its small size belies its great significance. The Commissioner and General Kujou discussed it thoroughly before selecting myself as the representative of the delegation.

response.speaker: Kuromaro
response.text: I was once in charge of leading a platoon to clear out the monsters and bandits in the mountains. I suffered few setbacks, and I considered my martial skills to be superb.

response.speaker: Kuromaro
response.text: Until the last "Warrior's Spirit Swordfighting Exhibition," in which my skills were edged out by Hirotatsu senpai, and I was unable to take part in the official competition. It was only then that I understood the meaning of humility...

response.speaker: Kuromaro
response.text: I was very fortunate that the Commissioner believed that although I could not reach the apex of swordsmanship, I could still lead soldiers into battle, and have great potential in the area of eradicating monsters. For this reason, I was gifted with this opportunity.

response.speaker: Kuromaro
response.text: It wasn't until after I came to Liyue that I realized that there is always someone out there who is better and that those with consummate martial prowess are beyond count. Just like Su Ding senpai, who is not only exceptional with the spear, but also a master of tactics.

choices.text: Truly, there are masters everywhere.

response.speaker: Kuromaro
response.text: Should there be a convenient juncture in the future, I hope you can recommend a few places suited towards expanding one's knowledge of martial disciplines to me. My gratitude would be beyond words!

choices.text: It's good to get out, travel, see the world, learn a bit.
Oh, stop it, you're embarrassing me...
What have you learned so far?

response.speaker: Kuromaro
response.text: My most profound understanding has been the balance between bravery and strategy.

response.speaker: Kuromaro
response.text: You should know well that Inazuma is a land of many islands, and when two sides clash, it often evolves into a series of groups of soldiers engaged in duels. In such situations, morale is of the utmost importance.

response.speaker: Kuromaro
response.text: In order to boost troop morale, the leader of the army must often take the lead, heroically charging the enemy with limitless courage. This seems to have almost become a convention.

response.speaker: Kuromaro
response.text: However, under the guidance of Su Ding senpai, I realized that if we follow such practices in every battle, then if faced with powerful monsters, the overall battlefield situation could spiral out of control.

response.speaker: Kuromaro
response.text: If, while leading my troops, I were to directly engage a... Thunderhelm Lawachurl, then I would certainly be hard-pressed, and might survive by the skin of my teeth. The morale of the other soldiers would plummet, and they might even panic.

response.speaker: Kuromaro
response.text: Therefore, strategy and bravery must be balanced. Though it may be difficult to form a continuous line of battle, cooperation between individual soldiers must be emphasized.

response.speaker: Kuromaro
response.text: Dividing and conquering, giving the order at the opportune moment, deciding as the leader when to advance and when to retreat... These are countless methods.

response.speaker: Kuromaro
response.text: If you do not mind, then please allow me to watch closely when you participate in the Wargames!

choices.text: Maybe next time!

response.speaker: Kuromaro
response.text: I understand, you are very busy! Please, take care, I shall be respectfully waiting for you here!

dialogues.speaker: Su Ding
dialogues.text: Thanks to your wargaming, most excellent commander, we've been able to compile a variety of different manuals that will provide great scenario-based training for soldiers of all ranks and specialisms. We are truly in your debt!

choices.text: I forgot to ask, you mentioned the Millelith General Staff...

response.speaker: Su Ding
response.text: Oh, that's just what we tend to call it. After all, it hasn't actually been around that long.

response.speaker: Su Ding
response.text: After the battle with Beisht, Lady Yuheng conferred with the other Qixing officers and decided it was high time to reorganize the Millelith's chain of command.

response.speaker: Su Ding
response.text: Liyue's had no lack of military advisers since ancient times, but most commander-strategists would work alone. The wisdom and influence that any one individual can bring to bear is, in truth, very limited.

response.speaker: Su Ding
response.text: Based on intel gathered from all over Teyvat, Lady Yuheng established this department as a way of bringing consultants and advisers together, streamlining the process of divvying up work.

response.speaker: Su Ding
response.text: This way, advisers will get to analyze more accurate intel so that the battle plans they create can be as watertight as possible. They'll also be able to hand over their findings to the troops with greater precision.

choices.text: Not sure I understand...

response.speaker: Su Ding
response.text: It's alright. Given your status, I suspect Lady Yuheng will explain it all to you in terms both comprehensive and comprehensible the next time you see her.

response.speaker: Su Ding
response.text: I also hope our intel will prove useful to you too, someday.

choices.text: Ah, I see...
Actually... What's "scenario-based training"?

response.speaker: Su Ding
response.text: It's a concept that the Lady Yuheng has been promoting, a product of synthesizing intel from multiple sources...

response.speaker: Su Ding
response.text: You can see it as a tool to help facilitate comprehensive assessment and training. It allows us to test a soldier's ability to organize, deploy, and command military forces from a variety of different angles.

response.speaker: Su Ding
response.text: The manuals might make for dense reading, though. The assessment process is stricter than with these tabletop Wargames, but there's much to be gained from running through the scenarios.

choices.text: That genuinely sounds very useful...

response.speaker: Su Ding
response.text: As the saying goes, "a talented commander never passes up an opportunity to hone their skills." All those soldiers' tales of your heroism are true!

response.speaker: Su Ding
response.text: Anyway, back to what we were talking about. Based on how these Wargames have panned out, writing up all the scenarios will likely be slow-going. I'll do my best, though.

choices.text: I think I'll pass...

response.speaker: Su Ding
response.text: No matter. I've heard that you've had a lot of very important things on your plate recently. Maybe you'll be willing to come try it out when you have the time.

choices.text: Very well, I'll leave you to it.

response.speaker: Su Ding
response.text: See you next time!

dialogues.speaker: Phonia
dialogues.text: Looks like you're pretty much done, Honorary Knight. Our work here is almost finished too, so we'll be heading back to Mondstadt soon.

choices.text: How did the collaboration go?

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: Not bad at all. It's exposed a flaw in our current strategy — namely, that the long-range capabilities of our mobile forces seem to be somewhat lacking.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: During the Wargames, we had multiple skirmishes with the clockwork meka of Fontaine. Though we did have units with heavy bows, they had great difficulty penetrating the thick armor of our opponents, so we had to get in close as much as possible.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: But as a result, we lost the intel advantage that we'd expected our alchemical recon equipment to give us.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: Seems like we're going to need the Outrider's input on this one.

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: Or... Perhaps Ematol could make us some miniature explosives, which we could... attach to our arrowheads?

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: Yes... That sounds like it might just work.

choices.text: Safe trip back!

response.speaker: Phonia
response.text: See you in Mondstadt, Honorary Knight.

dialogues.speaker: Turenna
dialogues.text: The Wargames are nearly over, Proto-Boss. Su Ding mentioned that your work all went pretty smoothly, yes?

choices.text: It did indeed! How's it all gone for you?

response.speaker: Turenna
response.text: It's been great, we've gotten so much out of it!

response.speaker: Turenna
response.text: In the Wargames, we came up against many highly mobile opponents, such as flying Fungi.

response.speaker: Turenna
response.text: Weapons like muskets, which are slow to fire and require precision, aren't very effective against such foes.

response.speaker: Turenna
response.text: To make up for this, we focused on improving our ability to implement rapid rotation tactics in smaller squads. Compared to our previous formation-based way of shooting, our combat style has become a lot more flexible!

response.speaker: Turenna
response.text: All in all, these Wargames have helped us identify weaknesses in our tactics, so we now have a much clearer idea of what we need to work on. I'm pumped, to be honest!

choices.text: That's great. See you next time!

response.speaker: Turenna
response.text: Yes, yes! And you're welcome to pay us a visit at the Special Security and Surveillance Patrol's headquarters at any time... if you can find it!

dialogues.speaker: Sido
dialogues.text: We meet again, friend of the General Mahamatra and the Flame-Mane. It's a shame that we can't stick around and chat for a few more days — we're preparing to return to Sumeru.

choices.text: How did the Wargames go?

response.speaker: Sido
response.text: The longer we spent doing it, the more we felt we learned.

response.speaker: Sido
response.text: For instance, we found ourselves facing monsters from Inazuma the likes of which we've rarely seen. Even with all our years of experience as mercenaries behind us, there was very little that could help us find an effective way to defeat them.

response.speaker: Sido
response.text: In the end, it was only after seeing the offensive strategies being used by others that we suddenly realized what we needed to do. It was like a revelation!

response.speaker: Sido
response.text: It must be said though, when you pit simulated monsters against one another like this, as long as you analyze the scenarios carefully enough...

response.speaker: Sido
response.text: There's always a way to ensure victory, even for a very averagely-equipped squad of Eremite mercenaries!

choices.text: Well then, see you in Sumeru!

response.speaker: Sido
response.text: Hahaha, yes! Next time we meet, I'll invite my brothers, the Flame-Mane, and even the General Mahamatra if possible, and we'll have a proper get-together!

dialogues.speaker: Kuromaro
dialogues.text: Esteemed guests of the Commissioner, it will soon be time for us to depart homeward. Seeing how busy you've been of late, I did not dare disturb you. If I have been remiss, please accept my apologies.

choices.text: No need to be so formal. You were here for the meeting after all!

response.speaker: Kuromaro
response.text: I am indeed here to learn, and thus it is only right that I should treat and address all the accomplished warriors present with the utmost humility.

response.speaker: Kuromaro
response.text: Fortunately, I can say with confidence that my attendance will not have disappointed the Commissioner's expectations. In the course of this trip, we have learned much and recorded many key findings.

response.speaker: Kuromaro
response.text: Based on these findings, the Shogun's Army will be able to focus on adapting their tactics, such that the vagrant ronin and bandits that roam our islands can be more efficiently dealt with...

response.speaker: Kuromaro
response.text: I only hope that, when the time is right, you will have a chance to visit Inazuma once more and witness the fruits of our labor.

choices.text: The pleasure would be all mine. Please give Ayato and Ayaka my regards!

response.speaker: Kuromaro
response.text: Your magnanimity has left a deep impression on me. I shall be sure to pass on your fine words to the Commissioner and Miss Kamisato!
